VERIFIED/HIGH. CORRECTED 2026-08-08 (Project Owner relay, Thangseng direct, supersedes this entry's original 2026-08-07 note): the original note wrongly implied bi·sa itself means 'young one'. Native clarification establishes bi·sa = 'offspring' (noun) and dambe = 'young' (adjective/modifier) as two DISTINCT morphemes, not one. 'dambe bi·sa' is therefore a literal compositional compound ('young' + 'offspring' = 'young offspring'), not bi·sa functioning alone as a generic young-one word. Productive pattern per native: animal + dambe = young [animal] (e.g. do·bok dambe = young goat); animal + bi·sa = baby/offspring of [animal] (e.g. do·bok bi·sa = kid, achak bi·sa = puppy). Human 'child'/'baby' senses of bare bi·sa are UNAFFECTED and remain correct. See NV-068.
